title: Stream-convergent admission stager for continuous batching and kernel-aware decode pacing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce 99th and 99.9th percentile tail latency for mixed short/long traffic by improving admission control and shaping of continuous batches, while selecting kernels and attention paths that minimize token processing variance.

Background: Current admission logic occasionally admits long-prefill requests into batches that force expensive kernel paths (full attention or large batch kernels), causing latency tail spikes and downstream QoS degradation. Previous efforts improved prefill gating but left some microbursts unhandled, and kernel selection is still conservative for safety.

Approach:
- Introduce a "stream-convergent" admission stage that temporarily buffers streams with ambiguous latency profiles and applies a short profiling prefill (up to N tokens or M ms) to classify as short/long/kv-heavy.
- Use profiling outcomes to route requests to kernel-aware batch lanes: small-seq fast-kernel lane, medium-kernel lane (quantized attention), and long-kernel lane with optimized KV cache management.
- Implement decode pacing: adaptive token emission that constrains decode step admission based on in-flight kernel budgets and measured variance.
- Attention optimizations: enable causal attention tiling and sparse-prefix hints for streams classified KV-heavy; fallback to dense attention only when necessary.

Success metrics:
- Reduce tail latency (P99) on mixed workload by >=25% relative to baseline for a target customer workload
- Reduce P99.9 by >=35% without increasing mean latency more than 5%
- Keep per-token cost within 3% of baseline

Deliverables:
- Design doc with microbench results and kernel mapping heuristics
- Feature flagged rollout with canary on dedicated clusters
- End-to-end dashboard (latency, kernel-util, token-cost) and an automated regression alert

Trade-offs and risks:
- Profiling prefill adds small extra cost and latency for short requests; tuning required to avoid regressions.
- Increased complexity in batch routing and lane maintenance may complicate debugging and allocations.
- Kernel mismatch errors if model variants are not available on every lane; requires fallback policies.

Open questions:
- Optimal profiling window size (tokens vs ms) for minimal overhead
- Interaction with autoscaling burst policies for Dedicated pools

comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff meeting: aligned on profiling-based classification. Action: Mateo to prototype micro-profiling harness.
2026-02-25 - Prototype results: 3-token profiling plus 2ms window correctly classifies 87% of short requests; edge cases for medium-length sequences observed.
2026-03-01 - Design review (ENG, SRE, PM): agreed to feature flag and canary gate. PM requested cost bucket estimates for export to billing metrics.
2026-03-05 - Engineering spike PR opened (runtime#8142). Initial microbench shows 18% P99 improvement in synthetic mixed workload.
2026-03-09 - Security review: no secrets required, KPI telemetry only. SRE noted potential increased memory churn on long-kernel lane; added as follow-up.
2026-03-12 - Canary started on two dedicated nodes (canary tags: canary/scs/2026-03). Observed P99 drop of 22% and P99.9 down 28% at 60% traffic; short-request mean increased 0.8ms.
2026-03-13 - PM feedback: prioritize fallback policy for lane kernel-unavailable errors. Added a subtask for cross-region kernel parity check (ENG-100234).
acceptance_criteria: Canary shows >=20% reduction on P99 and no more than 5% increase in short-request mean latency on a mixed workload
Automated fallback policy triggers and successfully routes when kernel variant is unavailable (test coverage in CI)
Dashboard shows kernel lane utilization and per-lane latency; alerts configured for regression relative to baseline
Feature flag toggles without requiring full restart or model reload
